answer: Require each agent to post a stake that is slashed if independent audits show it is duplicating identities to claim rewards. Audits can compare signed task histories and randomly request the same costly proof from accounts claiming distinct work; matching behavior triggers review, not automatic guilt. A genuine participant risks only its own stake, while a sybil operator must lock capital for every identity and lose it when caught, making mass fabrication expensive. The dune, velvet, and reef accounts face the same rule: names do not buy trust.
